violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: oyster sauce with cooked garlic at 86F at the cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CFM moved food to cooler.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed the handsink between the walk-in being used to thaw fish.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. The PIC corrected this during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Cover Foods in Storage
violations.observation: Unwrapped or uncovered food in the following location where the food is subject to contamination: several foods (tofu, tripe, others) stored in the walk-in were not covered.
violations.corrective_action: Foods shall be protected from contamination by being stored in packages, covered containers or wrappings unless being cooled. The PIC corrected this during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: custard tarts in the hot holding cabinets were 76º for 2 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. Custard products must be kept hot or cold. The PIC was advised to discard any unserved tarts after 2 hours. The PIC requested to put the tarts on time as a public health control. A TPHC policy was created during the inspection and will entered into the establishment record.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: several containers of sauces and other foods prepared on site were stored in the walk with no date marking.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. The PIC corrected this during the inspection. VINH KEE (Inspection Date: 03/30/2026) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: yellow and green desserts, cake desserts, cooked duck and chicken were all being held at room temperature with no temperature control. The PIC stated time as a public health control was being used by way of a timer, but the timer was not set. There was no record keeping for food expiration times.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. The manager was advised that when using time as a public health control, there must be some kind of record keeping to show when the 4-hour deadline is. The PIC said she would correct this.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: raw shrimp was being thawed at room temperature on the floor under the 3-compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. The PIC corrected this during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Foods were stored on the floor in the walk-in freezer. Foods (jellyfish, shrimp) were stored on the floor in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. Discontinue storing foods on the floor. Correct as soon as possible or within 90 days.

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found subject to contamination after receipt and during storage due to the condition as described: jellyfish was stored on the floor and under the 2-vat food prep sink; raw shrimp was being stored on the floor and under the three compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. The PIC corrected these during the inspection.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed clean pots stored on the floor under the handwashing sink located between the walk-in refrigerators.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. The PIC moved the clean pots during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk and produce crates were found being reused as. shelving in the kitchen, food storage in the refrigerators.
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. Discontinue reusing milk crates. Correct as soon as possible or within 90 days.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: aluminum foil was being used to line several sections of shelving in the kitchen. The foil was deteriorated and not clean.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. Removed the foil as soon as possible. Instead of using foil to line shelving, clean the shelving on a regular basis. VINH KEE (Inspection Date: 03/30/2026) Page 3 of 4

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: several refrigerator door handles had food and debris accumulated on them. The shelving in both walk-in refrigerators were visibly soiled and in need of cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Clean all refrigerator door handles especially the portions that employees touch with their fingers to open the doors. Correct as soon as possible or within 90 days.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: The left side faucet on the three compartment sink is leaking badly when the water is turned on, spraying out in several locations.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. Repair the leaking faucet as soon as possible or within 90 days.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed that most walls in the establishment were visibly soiled and in need of cleaning. The floor in the establishment was also visibly soiled and in need of cleaning, especially under the wok line and under all tables and refrigerators and equipment.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. Clean all walls and floors as soon as possible or within 90 days.

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observed several burnt out/non-working light bulbs in the kitchen ceiling light fixtures. These light fixtures are four bulb units, with most only having two bulbs work.
violations.corrective_action: Replace the burnt out bulbs so that all bulbs in all fixtures are working.

violations.title: Food Contact Surfaces Clean to Sight & Touch
violations.observation: The following equipment/utensils were observed soiled to sight and touch: strainer and mixing attachment and utensil hanging on the wall above the prep table were soiled and had food debris on them.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to the sight and touch. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. COOK TOOK ITEMS TO DISHWASHING AREA TO BE CLEANED AND SANITZED

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: barbecue pork bun 108F in 1 Door hot holding cabinet.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. COOK PLACED ITEM UNDER TIME AS A PUBLIC HEALTH CONTROL TO BE DISCARDED AFTER LUNCH; ALSO RAISED TEMPERATURE ON THE UNIT.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: raw chicken above raw pork in 2 dr upright cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). PIC placed raw chicken below raw pork.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: egg tart (72F), barbecue pork bun (103F) in 1 dr upright display warmer.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. PIC placed pork buns and egg tarts on time as a public health control.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: scoop at rice station observed stored in ambient temperature (76F) water.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC removed water from storage container and properly cleaned utensils.
